newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks snare record closes in "buying frenzy".
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks snare record closes in "buying frenzy".

text.p: Wall Street stock records were shattered as fresh economic data pointed to moderating economic growth and tame inflation, raising investor hopes of no Fed tightening soon and solid corporate profit growth.

"It was a buying frenzy based on the weaker-than-expected consumer prices and retail sales. The data clearly suggests the Fed does not need to raise interest rates at its upcoming September 24 FOMC meeting," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
The Dow industrials jumped 67 to an unofficial record 5839.
It was the Dow's first close above 5800 and topped the previous record high finish of 5778.00 scored on May 22.
The S&P 500 rose nine points to about 681, topping the previous record close of 678.51 set May 24.
The NYSE Composite surged four to about 363.70, near its all-time high finish of 363.74 scored May 24.

A powerful rally in technology shares helped send the tech-laden Nasdaq Composite up 23 to about 1189. It was the index's seventh biggest point gain in history, but still left it short of its record 1249.15 set June 5.
The long bond soared 1-17/32 to yield 6.95 percent.

Stock buyers were lured as the long bond yield fell below the key seven percent level. Bonds and stocks roared ahead after the consumer price index, closely watched by the Fed and Wall Street, rose 0.1 percent for August, below the expected 0.2 percent. August retail sales rose 0.2 percent, well below the anticipated 0.7 percent.

"Goldilocks is back -- the economy is not too hot or too cold," said David Shulman, chief equity strategist at Salomon Brothers. "This is the kind of environment where we'll have a Dow 6000 by the election."
The soothing CPI came after Thursday's tame PPI report.
Wins beat losses 17-7 on very heavy NYSE volume of about 486 million shares, the heaviest since July 17's 509 million.
"The buyers came and never left. A lot of people are piling on here now that we're in record territory," said Marty Kearney, a trader at PTI Securities.
William LeFevre, senior market analyst at Enhrenkrantz King Nussbaum, said the market's advance looked healthier.

"They're buying blue chip stocks. There was a time in 1995 and the first half of 1996 where it was high techs and it didn't matter if there were earnings. Then someone realized the emperor had no clothes," he said about the July tumble.
But many technology stocks powered ahead on Friday, bolstered by SoundView Financial's upgrade of the sector to near-term overweight from average.

IBM rallied 4-7/8 to 122-1/8, aiding the Dow's advance by about 15 points. Merrill Lynch upgraded IBM to near-term buy from accumulate, citing its recent mainframe and storage announcements as fueling strong earnings in the third and fourth quarters.
Oracle Corp, which reported stronger quarterly results, rose 4-5/8 to 42-1/8, Intel was up 2-3/4 to 88-1/8 and Hewlett-Packard added two to 46-1/2.
Microsoft, which rose 3-1/2 on Thursday, rose another 2-3/8 to 131. Motorola, which had been falling since Wednesday's profit warning, bounced back 7/8 to 48-5/8.

"Techs were by far the strongest group today. The Merrill and SoundView upgrades are part of that and our strategy of a massive corporate tech upgrade is beginning to gain acceptance within the marketplace," Value Line's Orlando said.

Interest-rate sensitive stocks were bolstered by the long bond yield's drop. Fannie Mae rose one to 34-5/8, Merrill Lynch added 1-1/8 to 64-1/4, Citicorp was up 2-1/4 to 88-1/2 after touching a year-high 89 and AMR rose 1-3/4 to 80-7/8.
LeFevre noted that the Investment Company Institute on Wednesday estimated August inflows to stock mutual funds at $19 billion.

"People are still thowing money in, whether through 401ks or through money managers," he said. "The fundamentals are there. Third-quarter earnings would appear to be a lot better than expected. Higher earnings absent inflation usually mean higher stock prices." Among individual shares, Gillette surged 4-3/8 to 70-3/8 after a Goldman Sachs upgrade. Duracell rose 4-1/2 to 62-3/4. On Thursday, Duracell jumped 9-7/8 and Gillette one after they agreed to merge.
Xerox continued lower, off 1-1/4 to 53-3/8. The shares lost three on Thursday after news it ended a pact to sell its Talegen insurance businesses to a KKR group.

Optical Data slumped 4-5/8 to 18-5/8. Volpe Welty said it cut the stock to buy on concern it will not meet Volpe Welty's third-quarter share estimate of $0.30 after a conversation with the company. Optical Data was not available.
For the week, the Dow jumped 178.66 points, the second biggest weekly point gain ever after the August 2 week's 206.77. The Nasdaq Composite rose 22.86 to 1188.67.
The S&P 500 index rose 9.41 to 680.54.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk, 212 859 1721
